caption: Fixes #1924: a routing block's riders who fall behind their places as its flight turns and gathers pace now keep up. A 64-horse squadron, already broken, flees north (up the screen) toward a long wall that stands across its whole line of flight, so its flight turns north-west onto a detour toward the wall's west end while it speeds up; no rider reaches the wall. A rider more than 3 m off his place may now change his speed and direction faster than usual, by as much as what he follows is changing (his place's own movement plus any sidestep off a friendly block), while that is not slowing, at most twice his usual rate on top. Measured on this clip: at the end the farthest rider is 73 wu (3.6 m) from his place and none is more than a rank's distance (120 wu, 6 m) off at any sampled tick. Before the fix the farthest rider ended 166 wu (8.3 m) behind, with 2 riders more than a rank's distance off. The clip ends just before the rout timer runs out and the squadron rallies.
